messages.subject: Re: Estimate effects
messages.body_plain:
For autosomes in a backcross or intercross, if you use the argument
get.ests=TRUE in fitqtl(), you'll get such coefficient estimates.
It's not working properly for the X chromosome....well, it gets
estimates correctly, but the coding is essentially without meaning.

The coding I'm using is the following:

   Backcross:   1/2 for A, -1/2 for H

   Intercross:  a: -1 for A, 0 for H, +1 for B
                d: -1/2 for A, +1/2 for H, -1/2 for B

karl

messages.subject: Multiple phenotypes
messages.body_plain:
If there are multiple phenotypes, which one does R/qtl use to run the
QTL analysis?  Is it possible to designate which phenotype you want the
program to use?
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Re: Multiple phenotypes
messages.body_plain:
In scanone and scantwo, there is an argument "pheno.col" through which
one specifies which column in the phenotype data should be used.

karl

messages.subject: LOD scores
messages.body_plain:
If there are two peaks on a chromosome, is it possible to print out the
LOD score for both of these peaks?  When I do the summary(out.em) it
only prints the top LOD for each chromosome.

Thanks!
messages.body_snippet:
If there are two peaks on a chromosome, is it possible to print out the
LOD score for both of these peaks?  When I do the summary(out.em) it
only prints the top LOD for each chromosome.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: LOD scores
messages.body_plain:
There isn't an easy way at this point.  If "out.em" is your output,
you could type

   out.em[out.em[,1]==3,]

to look at all of the results for chromosome 3.

karl
